title: Review: Damping, forced oscillations and resonance; Rutherford scattering and atomic models; Nuclear radius and density; Radioactive decay: types and properties
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q06-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; Q07-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; Q07-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; Q07-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N02-1#N.5, O04-uk1#N.10, Q06-1#N.14a, Q07-1#N.10, N02-1#N.13, O04-uk1#N.3, Q06-1#N.4, Q07-1#N.6, N02-1#N.10a, O04-uk1#N.5, Q06-1#N.7a, Q07-1#N.7. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Atom
items.clue: About 10⁻¹⁰ m across: roughly 10⁴ to 10⁵ times wider than its positive core.

items.label: Nuclear radius
items.clue: About 2.7 fm for carbon-12 and 7.4 fm for uranium-238; it doubles when A rises 8 times.

items.label: Nuclear density
items.clue: About 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ whatever the value of A, some 10¹³ times that of ordinary solids.

items.label: Nucleon number
items.clue: Symbol A, 197 for gold-197; mass is proportional to it, so it cancels in mass over volume.

questions.stem: A nucleus has nucleon number A and proton number Z. It undergoes an alpha decay, and the nucleus formed then undergoes a beta-minus decay. Which expression gives the number of neutrons in the final nucleus?
A car's wing mirror buzzes violently at one engine speed. A rubber damper is fitted to the mirror's mounting. What happens now as the engine passes that speed?

options.text: The violent buzzing moves to a much higher engine speed.
The mirror stops responding to the engine at all.
It still buzzes most near the same engine speed, but far less.
It now buzzes strongly at every engine speed.

questions.explanation: Damping removes energy every cycle. The resonance peak stays at about the same frequency but is much lower (and broader).

questions.stem: A gold nucleus is about 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁴ m across and a gold atom is about 2.9 × 10⁻¹⁰ m across. In a scale drawing the nucleus is a dot 1 mm across. How wide must the atom be drawn?
A neutron star has a mass of 2.8 × 10³⁰ kg. Model it as a sphere of nuclear matter, with the same density as any nucleus. Estimate its radius.
Thorium-232 (²³²₉₀Th) decays through a chain of α and β⁻ decays to stable lead-208 (²⁰⁸₈₂Pb). How many α decays and how many β⁻ decays are there in the chain?

A lightly damped mass–spring system is released with an amplitude of 60 mm. After one complete oscillation its amplitude is 45 mm. The amplitude falls by the same fraction in each oscillation. What is the amplitude after three complete oscillations?
questions.explanation: Each amplitude is 0.75 × the previous one: 60 × 0.75³ = 25 mm.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which statement about the results of the Geiger–Marsden–Rutherford alpha-particle scattering experiment is correct?

options.text: Most of the alpha particles were deflected through large angles, and only a few passed straight through.
Nearly all the alpha particles passed through almost undeflected; a very few were deflected by more than 90°.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had collided with the electrons in the gold atoms.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had struck the hard outer surface of a gold nucleus.

questions.stem: A nucleus of lead-208 has proton number 82 and nucleon number 208. Using r = r₀A^(1/3) with r₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, what is the radius of this nucleus?
A steel works checks the thickness of steel sheet, about 5 mm thick, with a radioactive source on one side of the sheet and a detector on the other. Which type of source is most suitable, and why?

options.text: α, as it is the most strongly ionising, so the steel absorbs it strongly.
β⁻, as β⁻ is partly absorbed by thin sheets, as in gauging paper.
γ, as only γ passes through 5 mm of steel, partly absorbed.
α, as its range of a few cm is greater than the 5 mm thickness of the sheet.

questions.explanation: The source must be partly absorbed: some must reach the detector, and the count must fall as the sheet thickens. Only γ does both for 5 mm of steel.

questions.stem: Damping reduces the amplitude of a mass–spring oscillator from 40 mm to 20 mm. What fraction of the original oscillation energy has been transferred to the surroundings?

options.text: None, because the period has not changed

questions.explanation: E ∝ A². Half the amplitude leaves 1/4 of the energy, so 3/4 has been transferred to the surroundings.

questions.stem: A gold nucleus has radius 7.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and a gold atom has radius 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. Roughly what fraction of the atom's volume does the nucleus occupy?
questions.explanation: (7.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ ÷ 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰)³ = (5.0 × 10⁻⁵)³ = 1.25 × 10⁻¹³. The atom is almost entirely empty space.

questions.stem: A carbon-12 nucleus contains 12 nucleons, each of mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. r₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. What is the density of the nucleus?
questions.explanation: Radius = 2.75 × 10⁻¹⁵ m; V = ⁴⁄₃π(radius)³ = 8.69 × 10⁻⁴⁴ m³; m = 2.00 × 10⁻²⁶ kg; ρ = m/V = 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.
